title: AI May Deepen Justice System Gaps, Law Society Warns
source_used: Legal Futures (Law360 page returned no text)
key_facts: The Law Society predicts agentic AI (AI that takes actions on a person's behalf) could become the 'default doorway' into the justice system.
Researchers say this could be either the 'largest expansion of legal capability in history' or justice could become something people subscribe to or are excluded from.
Agentic AI is not yet deployed in the justice system, but 'the conditions for its emergence are beginning to develop'.
The report reviewed China, the US, Estonia and the UK and interviewed 19 AI-in-law practitioners and 11 justice-system experts.
It warns regulation 'may be trying to govern yesterday's technology' and that accountability 'may arrive after harm rather than before it'.
The Law Society calls for clear accountability, transparency, meaningful human oversight and public debate before widespread use.
Vice-president Brett Dixon: 'Legal judgement cannot be delegated.'
quote_evidence: Though agentic AI was not yet deployed in the justice system, “the conditions for its emergence are beginning to develop” in the coming years.
The Law Society said it was calling for clear accountability for agentic AI in justice, transparency of AI decision-making, “meaningful human oversight”, and public debate before widespread use.
why_it_matters_hint: A professional body warns that AI could gate access to justice and wants safeguards first.
notes: Law360 original (paywalled/no text) not read; read Legal Futures, which covers the Law Society report. Law Society described as the solicitors' body of England and Wales from general knowledge (it is the Law Society).
